title: Understand your shell environment
goal: Explain local versus exported values and restore a temporary command-search path.
challenge: Demonstrate a local variable absent from a child Bash, an exported value visible there, command lookup, and a temporary PATH change. Restore the exact original PATH and remove only your practice variables. Do not edit login files.

steps.explanation: Create a unique learner-owned guest workspace. Stop if creation or cd fails. Retain its printed path; variables do not survive disk Resume.
steps.expected: A fresh directory inside the guest home; no existing files are changed.

steps.command: saved_path=$PATH; note='local value'; unset LAB_NOTE; type printf; printf '<%s>\n' "$note"
steps.explanation: Save PATH before any change. type reveals builtins as well as external commands.
steps.expected: printf is a builtin here; note has a space.

steps.explanation: A shell variable is not automatically in a newly executed child environment. ${name-default} handles unset values.

steps.command: LAB_NOTE='child value'; export LAB_NOTE; bash -c 'printf "child LAB_NOTE=<%s>\n" "$LAB_NOTE"'
steps.explanation: Export affects future children, not a parent shell. Do not store secrets in this exercise.

steps.command: PATH=/usr/bin:/bin; export PATH; type -a printf; command -v bash; /usr/bin/printf '%s\n' absolute
steps.explanation: This change is temporary in the practice shell. An absolute pathname bypasses PATH lookup.

steps.command: PATH=$saved_path; export PATH; unset LAB_NOTE note; printf 'PATH restored=%s\n' "$PATH"
steps.explanation: Restore exactly; no .bashrc, profile or global configuration edits.

hints: Why can a child inherit an exported value but not change its parent?
Compare actual output, immediate exit status and resulting files. A syntactically valid command or script can still do the wrong thing.
Keep the original, verify a small intended change, and demonstrate rollback inside this workspace.
review: I retained the stated observations and can explain the outcome.
I checked failure cases and preserved originals; my review is not an application-verified score.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 partial 103.1, 105.1 partial environment. Reinforcement is labeled; no full-objective mastery. Completion records self-review, not verified assessment. No score.
